We Code, Solve & WIN.
summary:
HardToFind is a web-based astronomical search and visualization tool that makes deep-sky infrared research accessible to everyone — not just professional astronomers.

It addresses the challenge of finding hard-to-detect objects — brown dwarfs, rogue planets, and hypothetical Planet Nine candidates — by integrating three NASA data sources into a single interface: SPHEREx (102-band infrared spectroscopy), WISEView (time-lapse sky animations), and Firefly Viewer (FITS image analysis).

Its core feature is a custom filter engine that processes sky coordinates across SPHEREx’s infrared spectrum (0.75 µm to 5.0 µm), enabling targeted queries for cold, faint, and fast-moving objects. Pre-configured test targets — Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, and WISE 0855 — help calibrate and validate observations.

HardToFind empowers citizen scientists, students and researchers to contribute to the search for undiscovered objects at the outer edges of our solar system.
details:
Our project works in three layers:

1. Data Aggregation — Pulls infrared sky data from NASA's SPHEREx mission (102 spectral bands from 0.75 µm to 5.0 µm), WISE time-lapse archives via WISEView, and professional FITS image inspection through Firefly Viewer.

2. Filter Engine — Users input sky coordinates (RA/DEC) and the tool processes them through a custom SIA (Simple Image Access) query API, filtering results by specific spectral bands and calculating thermal flux estimates and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR).

3. Visualization — Results are rendered through motion animations (WISEView) and multi-band spectral analysis (Firefly), allowing users to detect proper motion, infrared emission peaks, and chemical/thermal signatures of faint objects.

Pre-configured target presets — Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aur, and R Lep — are built in to help users calibrate observations and understand expected outputs.

Benefits

  • Accessibility — Anyone with a browser can query NASA infrared data; no specialized software or institutional access required.
  • Education — Interactive spectrum explorer and preset targets make infrared astronomy hands-on.
  • Multi-mission integration — SPHEREx, WISEView, and Firefly Viewer combined into a single, unified workflow instead of three separate tools.

Intended Impact

HardToFind aims to democratize access to frontier space research.

Tools that we used

  • Core & Backend: Python (data processing & API routing with vercel), Vanilla JavaScript (frontend logic & i18n), HTML5/CSS3.
  • Hosting & Backend: Vercel (backend) and Firebase (frontend).
  • UI & Design: Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, and Google Fonts (Inter & JetBrains Mono).
  • Astronomy Tools: NASA SPHEREx SIA API , WISEView (motion animations), and Firefly Viewer (FITS image inspection).
  • UX & Standards: FITS data format, CSS Keyframes + Intersection Observer (scroll animations)

How Is It Creative?

  • Bridging worlds — WISEView's motion animations and Firefly's FITS inspector — normally researcher-only tools — wrapped in a friendly, accessible interface.
  • Preset-driven onboarding — Rather than presenting a blank search field, the tool offers real calibration targets with known coordinates and object types, turning the first interaction into a learning experience.
  • Bridging citizen science and professional tools — Connecting WISEView's motion GIFs and Firefly's FITS inspector — tools typically reserved for researchers — into a guided, friendly interface that anyone can use.

Factors the Team Considered

  • Usability vs. depth — Clean UI without sacrificing technical detail (RA/DEC, µm wavelengths).
  • Performance — Dependency-light for low-bandwidth users in Angola and other developing regions.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • Assistance & Logic: Used Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT to draft JavaScript/Python logic (SkyCoords/SIA queries), write multi-language UI copy (PT/EN), and optimize documentation.
  • Data & Prototyping: Streamlined NASA SPHEREx spectral data filtering via Python with AI assistance, and rapidly structured the web interface using modern prototyping tools.
  • Integrity: AI accelerated development cycles, but all scientific research, core architecture, coordinate filtering, and design direction were 100% conceived and controlled by the team.
